ayahOccurrences.text: وَلَوْ شِئْنَا لَرَفَعْنَٰهُ بِهَا وَلَٰكِنَّهُۥٓ أَخْلَدَ إِلَى ٱلْأَرْضِ وَٱتَّبَعَ هَوَىٰهُ ۚ فَمَثَلُهُۥ كَمَثَلِ ٱلْكَلْبِ إِن تَحْمِلْ عَلَيْهِ يَلْهَثْ أَوْ تَتْرُكْهُ يَلْهَث ۚ ذَّٰلِكَ مَثَلُ ٱلْقَوْمِ ٱلَّذِينَ كَذَّبُوا۟ بِـَٔايَٰتِنَا ۚ فَٱقْصُصِ ٱلْقَصَصَ لَعَلَّهُمْ يَتَفَكَّرُونَ

lexSnapshot.wordGrammar: 3rd person masculine singular imperfect verb, jussive mood
lexSnapshot.derivativeNote: يَلْهَثْ is in the derivative form: يَلْهَث
lexSnapshot.rootDefinitionHtml:
ل/ﻫ/ﺙ   l–h–th the physical sensation of thirst, panting with thirst, panting; to loll the tongue; fatigue. Of this root, only يَلْهَث yalhath occurs 2 times in the Qur’an
.
lexSnapshot.mainDefinitionHtml:
يَلْهَث yalhath [imperf. v., intrans.] to pant with thirst, to hang one’s tongue out, panting

(7:176) أَوْ‏ ‏فَمَثَلُهُ‏ ‏كَمَثَلِ‏ ‏الْكَلْبِ‏ ‏إِنْ‏ ‏تَحْمِلْ‏ ‏عَلَيْهِ‏ ‏يَلْهَثْ‏ ‏‏تَتْرُكْهُ‏ ‏يَلْهَثْ so his likeness is that of a dog: attack him, and he pants [with his tongue out]; leave him alone, and he pants [with his tongue out].
